title: Preserve authenticated initial intake heads during reconciliation
body:
## Summary

- Preserve the authenticated initial observation for revised intake PRs #3107, #3184 and #3251. At canonical `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, the ledger retains each original `starting_head`, but mutable intake metadata describes a later head. The checker rejects these legitimate records, and a complete generator run incorrectly replaces their initial heads with the current heads.
- Share one Git-free checkpoint adapter between generator and checker. It authenticates four existing receipt files by exact SHA-256, selects the PR-specific original-head field, and verifies current/reviewed head, metadata number and contributor against the authenticated receipt. Original observations were independently checked against their first committed intake records: `82d67beb`, `09fbc0f0` and `24db9bff`. No ledger, intake, receipt, frozen source, selected result or source pin is changed.
- Add rejection controls and watch the exact new helper, test and receipt dependencies in the existing tooling workflow. This is an explicit adapter for the current checkpoint: changed receipt bytes or another revision of these three PRs fail closed and require reviewed maintenance. Future intake needs a durable immutable initial-observation pin; unverified ledger history is never a fallback.

Credit Douglas R. Colkitt's reconciliation/intake infrastructure, roife's [PR704](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/704) for metadata binding, and the retained Gonzalo Mier / rohanarun contribution records. This contribution repairs offline provenance checking, not scientific results or live GitHub state.

## Test plan

- [x] CPython 3.12.14, macOS 27 arm64: all 7 new tests pass normally and with `-O`, with warnings treated as errors. They execute the actual generator and checker metadata boundary, preserve current head/reviewed head/attribution, and reject forged initial/current heads, future revisions, metadata substitutions and changed receipt bytes.

  ```sh
  python3.12 -B -W error -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_pr_reconciliation_initial_heads.py' -v
  python3.12 -B -W error -O -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_pr_reconciliation_initial_heads.py' -v
  ```

- [x] Independent complete generator comparison, with writes intercepted in memory: exactly three `starting_head` values change across 3,028 rows; every other JSON value and the complete Markdown output remain identical. No generated artifact was written.
- [x] Independent code/source-binding review; no live registered `SOURCES.json` or `VERIFY.json` pin needs modification. Historical evidence remains unchanged.
- [x] In a disposable complete integration tree with this change plus exact pending [PR3648](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3648) (`a0d88d68`), [PR3686](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3686) (`932f3b1`) and [PR3688](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3688) (`3463ba61`), all 38 reconciliation tests pass in both modes. Both new files are included in the tracked inventory used by the historical wrapper. Those other PR changes are not included here.

  ```sh
  python3.12 -B -W error -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_pr_reconciliation*.py' -v
  python3.12 -B -W error -O -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_pr_reconciliation*.py' -v
  ```

- [x] Ran `python3.12 -B scripts/replay_historical_check.py tooling-ledger` once on that combined tree, capped at 600 seconds. It passes the former initial-head failure and the family checks through batch1047, then exits after 29.76 seconds at the separate existing PR1048 review-completion mismatch: batch1099's historical flags/evidence differ from the later ledger record. The untouched canonical checker reproduces that failure directly. No validation bypass or data rewrite was added.
- [ ] Full tooling CI is not green: it needs the pending compatibility fixes above and separate resolution of the existing PR1048 mismatch. No complete historical-ledger replay success or Linux execution is claimed.

Prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance for investigation, implementation, tests, execution, independent agent review and writing. Apache-2.0.


Hosted follow-up (2026-10-19 JST): the [fork push run](https://github.com/roger-sato/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39140967700) at `af040ab4` passes the exact tooling and scoped owner/provenance steps, then stops before the reconciliation unit tests at the unchanged `docs/ci-verification.md` source-admission guard addressed by PR3648. Thus the new reconciliation tests and combined 38-test result above remain local evidence. Upstream pull-request Actions require maintainer approval; no full Linux ledger success is claimed.
